terms.gloss: the Roman copper coin; a penny, in sayings
evidence: Hor. Ep. 2.2.27: ad assem, to the last penny
terms.comment: The smallest everyday coin, and so the penny of proverbs: not worth a penny, ūnius assis; to the last penny, ad assem.

phrases.latin: nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs
phrases.english: “Don’t hold it out,” he said, “as if you were giving a penny to an elephant” (Augustus, to a man nervously handing him a petition)

sources: Lewis & Short: as
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 106, 130.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. euro (currency of European Union); s.v. penny, cent (U.S., European), also dēnārius.
Catullus and Quintilian from the Latinitas loci collections; Horace as Lewis & Short quotes him (s.v. as).
